negative_findings.description: No publicly browsable, case-level register of Hungarian collective-redundancy (csoportos létszámleépítés) notifications was found. NFSZ documents the ESTAT electronic filing system and names the receiving kormányhivatal, but the filings themselves appear to be administrative, not published per-employer.
negative_findings.result_summary: Only aggregate statistics and secondary press round-ups (HR Portál) surfaced; no per-bank filing feed.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: The strongest legally-compelled negative signal for this cell is not directly harvestable; collection must rely on aggregates plus press reconstruction, or a freedom-of-information request.

negative_findings.description: Multiple independent Hungarian sources (mfor/Privátbankár survey, money.hu) report that branch-network contraction has NOT been matched by workforce contraction: branches fell from 1401 (start 2025) to 1268 (31 March 2026) while credit-institution employment rose above 40,500.
negative_findings.result_summary: Branch closures and headcount reduction are decoupled in the current Hungarian cycle.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Using branch closures as a proxy for layoffs would produce false positives; the cell needs separate indicators for network cuts vs. workforce cuts.

negative_findings.description: The BBDSZ federation web presence (bbdsz.hu) appears dated and the search surface returned mainly historical material (founding congress 1989, general aims) rather than current bargaining or restructuring statements. No current bank-level collective agreement text was located on it.
negative_findings.result_summary: Sectoral federation is identifiable but its site did not yield recent primary documents in this pass.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: The named union in the seed query may be a weaker live signal than the newer company-level unions (e.g. the UniCredit union under Munkástanácsok). Do not record bbdsz.hu as dead on this evidence — it is unverified.

negative_findings.description: No evidence was found of an active, published, sector-wide collective agreement (ágazati kollektív szerződés) for Hungarian banking, nor of publicly posted works-council (üzemi tanács) minutes at OTP, Erste, K&H or MBH.
negative_findings.result_summary: Only generic KSZ templates and general legal commentary surfaced; company-level agreement texts were not public.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Collective-agreement content for named banks will likely require union contact, leaked/press copies, or FOI — it is not an automatable open source.

negative_findings.description: BBDSZ (Bankok és Biztosítók Dolgozóinak Szakszervezeti Szövetsége) and BDDSZ (bddsz.hu) are near-identical acronyms belonging to different organisations; BRDSZ and VPDSZ also appear in the same result sets and are unrelated public-sector unions.
negative_findings.result_summary: Search on the seed acronym returns several unrelated unions.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: High risk of misattributing statements to the banking union; the actor map must pin each union by registry ID and domain.

negative_findings.description: The Hungarian phrase 'bankfiók bezárás' is heavily polluted by consumer content about closing a bank ACCOUNT ('bankszámla megszüntetés') and by branch-opening-hours pages; 'leépítés' also returns IT/system decommissioning content.
negative_findings.result_summary: Seed-style queries return substantial consumer-advice noise.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Collection queries must be constrained with employer names, 'fiókhálózat', 'hálózatszűkítés', or NFSZ/legal terms to keep precision.

coverage_gaps.description: Case-level collective-redundancy notifications filed via ESTAT to county/Budapest government offices are not open data.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: File a kozerdeku adatigenyles (FOI request) with NFSZ or the Budapest Fővárosi Kormányhivatal for anonymised/sectoral breakdowns of NACE-K collective redundancy notifications; test whether any kormanyhivatal publishes them locally.

coverage_gaps.description: Only the UniCredit Bank Hungary company union was clearly identified as a live, active company-level union in banking. Equivalent bodies at OTP, MBH, Erste, K&H, Raiffeisen, CIB and Gránit were not located in this pass.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Snowball from the Munkástanácsok / LIGA / MASZSZ affiliate lists and the szakszervezetek.hu union database; cross-check each against the civil-organisation registry (birosag.hu civil szervezetek névjegyzéke).

coverage_gaps.description: The official Hungarian civil-organisation registry (birosag.hu civil szervezetek névjegyzéke) and the official company register (e-cegjegyzek / Cégközlöny) were not directly searched in this pass; only the commercial aggregator Céginfo was found.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Add a dedicated probe of birosag.hu and e-cegjegyzek/Cégközlöny for finance-sector unions and for bank entity mergers/branch deregistrations.

coverage_gaps.description: Annual reports / e-beszámoló filings of individual Hungarian banks, which carry audited average headcount figures, were not probed; only MBH's disclosure page and bond prospectus were reached.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Probe e-beszamolo.im.gov.hu and each bank's investor-relations page for per-entity average staff numbers; build a per-bank annual headcount series to detect quiet contraction.

coverage_gaps.description: No source of Hungarian labour-court decisions (birosag.hu anonimizált határozatok) was assessed, although the UniCredit union-president dismissal is explicitly heading to court.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Add the anonymised court decision collection as a candidate source and set a watch on finance-sector labour disputes.

coverage_gaps.description: English-language coverage of Hungarian bank workforce contraction is thin and mostly routed through Eurofound ERM; no Hungarian-focused English trade outlet (e.g. BBJ, Telex English) was confirmed as a systematic source.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Probe Budapest Business Journal and English-language Hungarian outlets for restructuring coverage to serve non-Hungarian-reading consumers of this stream.

brief: The negative-signal half of A5 in Hungary rests on three distinct layers: a statutory layer (NFSZ/ESTAT collective-redundancy notifications and the underlying Mt. rules) that is legally compelled but not published case-by-case, a quantitative layer (MNB Aranykönyv per-institution branch and headcount series, KSH NACE-K employment, and the recurring mfor/Privátbankár bank-by-bank survey) that is fully open and machine-collectable, and a contested layer (Munkástanácsok, BBDSZ, UNI Europa, and press) where disputes surface as narrative rather than documents. The most important finding is that branch closures and workforce cuts are currently decoupled in Hungary — branches fell from 1401 to 1268 between early 2025 and Q1 2026 while sector employment rose above 40,500 — so network contraction must not be used as a layoff proxy. Eurofound's European Restructuring Monitor is the only structured, case-level, cross-checkable database found for named Hungarian bank restructuring events, and the newly unionised UniCredit Bank Hungary workforce (with its president dismissed in April 2026 and litigation pending) is the live focal conflict to watch. Main gaps: no open case-level redundancy filings, no per-bank union map beyond UniCredit, and unprobed official registries (birosag.hu, e-cegjegyzék, e-beszámoló) that would yield audited headcount and entity-level structural change.
